question.text: Active fixed-income managers track three aspects of the yield curve — the '3S'. Which of the following is NOT one of them?

explanation.text: The Logic: The 3S are Shift, Slope, Shape. Sector is a cross-sectional concept, not a yield-curve-movement axis. The Trap: Sector is relevant for corporate bond strategies, but the '3S' refers specifically to yield-curve movement. Cross-Exam Context: IV and XIII use 3S; XXI-B tests recall. Manager's Pro-Tip: Most alpha in FI PM comes from correctly calling one or two of the 3Ss — not all three. Specialisation beats generalisation here.
